content:
sylvie: kicking off a quick sanity pack for the Lyra LoRA merge for customer Aurora. goal: compatibility + 4bit quant smoke. running on a small eval shard first. pinging @jake and @maria if you want to piggyback.

jake: thanks — can you drop the merge diff + model hashes? want to check KV cache offsets and tokenizer special tokens.

sylvie: sure. diffs are tiny — LoRA weights stitched into base@v1.2.3 -> merged@v1.2.3-lora. hashes: base: sha256:aa11..., merged: sha256:bb22...

maria: noted. I’ll run the quickpack (intent, dialog, and few-shot summarization) in 4-bit and fp16 for baseline.

# command I ran to spawn the quickpack

```bash
./tools/quick_eval.sh --model artifacts/merged@v1.2.3-lora --quant=4bit --tasks quickpack_aurora --out ./evals/aurora/lyra_4bit.json 
```

maria: initial run finished locally. latency looks fine but one mismatch on polite-request edgecases (response truncation). attaching a diff snippet: `resp[23]` shorter by ~12 tokens vs fp16.

jake: can you paste an example? might be kv-cache alignment or generation stopping criteria. also what sampling params?

maria: sampling: top_p=0.92, temp=0.2, max_new_tokens=128, stop_tokens=["

"]. example: input: "Please summarize the meeting but keep private notes separate." fp16 -> "...and flag private items for follow-up." 4bit -> "...and flag private" (truncated).

sylvie: hmmm. that pattern smells like a tokenization boundary or EOS id mismatch. did we preserve special_ids when merging?

jake: quick check: tokenizer config shows eos_id=50256 in base, merged preserved. but adapter merge script may have rewritten pad token index mapping. can you run fast check: `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('artifacts/merged@v1.2.3-lora'); print(t.eos_token_id, t.pad_token_id)"`

maria: ran it: eos=50256 pad=1. looks OK. ops-bot: noticed that the 4bit conversion used blockwise quant config A instead of B; maybe different attention kernel fallback.

ops-bot: deploy log: conversion step used quant_profile: blockA_v2 because quant_metadata.profile was missing, defaulted. Suggest re-run quantize with profile=blockB_compat which keeps remat path.

maria: re-queued 4bit quant with profile=blockB_compat. re-run started: job id q-3821.

eval-bot: quickpack run complete (q-3821). metrics: rougeL_fp16=0.48, rougeL_4bit_old=0.44, rougeL_4bit_blockB=0.47. token_trunc_mismatch reduced from 12->1 instances.

sylvie: great, looks like blockB is the winner. next steps: 1) add quant_profile=blockB_compat to merge CI; 2) add small unit test for polite-request truncation; 3) push eval artifacts to bucket and notify Aurora.

jake: I'll open the PR for CI change and add the unit test.

maria: I’ll upload evals to s3://redwood-evals/aurora/lyra/1832105678/ and tag with run=q-3821. leaving notes in the eval summary.

sylvie: perfect. tagging this thread for follow-up during tomorrow sync. thanks all :thumbsup:
